title: Cardiac arrest
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Fictional scenario specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.
learning_objectives: Recognise cardiac arrest and call the team and start compressions without delay.
Keep the pre-shock pause as short as possible.
Perform and call the safety check before a shock.
Know that defibrillator operation is limited to authorised roles.

sources.use: ERC ALS 2025 (paraphrase only; commercial use needs an agreement)

required_sources: Unit resuscitation policy and the authorised-role requirements
gaps: No published clinical scenario may exist until the review phase: this is a specification only.
The branching content, consequences and scoring are the author's reading of the cited sources and have had no clinical review.
Rhythm analysis, energy selection, drugs and post-arrest care are deliberately outside this scenario.
Authorised-role requirements for defibrillation are local.
permissions: Cited sources are paraphrased only; see the licensing register for each source's reproduction status.
ERC text: commercial agreement required; AHA: permission required.
setting: A fictional adult found unresponsive on a fictional unit with a monitor and defibrillator.

steps.info: A patient is unresponsive and not breathing normally.

options.text: Call the team and start chest compressions without delay in line with the unit's procedure.
options.feedback: Recognising the arrest, calling the team and starting compressions without delay is the expected response.
options.consequence: Compressions are under way and the team and defibrillator are coming.

options.text: Fetch the defibrillator first and start compressions when you return.
options.feedback: Equipment is needed, but compressions should not wait for it.
options.consequence: The patient has no circulation while you fetch the machine.

options.text: Wait for a senior to arrive before doing anything.
options.feedback: Waiting delays treatment; call for help and start compressions.

steps.info: The defibrillator arrives while compressions continue.
steps.prompt: How should the pads and the pause be handled?

options.text: Apply the pads as soon as the defibrillator arrives and keep compressions going while it charges, keeping the pre-shock pause as short as possible.
options.feedback: Pads are preferred, compressions continue while charging, and even a short extra delay reduces the chance of shock success; operation is for authorised roles.
options.consequence: The defibrillator is ready with minimal interruption to compressions.

options.text: Stop compressions until the defibrillator has charged.
options.feedback: Stopping while charging lengthens the pre-shock pause.
options.consequence: The pause is long and the chance of success falls.

options.text: Use the paddles without checking contact because they are quicker.
options.feedback: Pads are preferred; if paddles are used, firm force and good contact are needed.
options.consequence: Poor contact risks arcing and an ineffective shock.

steps.info: The authorised operator is ready to deliver a shock.
steps.prompt: What must happen before the shock?

options.text: Perform and call the safety check so nobody touches the patient or bed, and follow the unit's oxygen safety steps.
options.feedback: A safety check protects everyone at the moment of the shock; oxygen safety steps are part of unit policy.
options.consequence: The shock is delivered safely and compressions restart at once.

options.text: Deliver the shock while a colleague continues manual compressions, wearing gloves.
options.feedback: A shock must not be given during manual compressions, even with gloves.
options.consequence: A colleague is put at risk of injury.

options.text: Shout 'clear' once without looking around the bed.
options.feedback: A call is part of the check, but the check must include looking so that nobody is touching the patient or bed.
options.consequence: The shock is delivered but a colleague's hand was still on the bed rail.

learning_points: Call the team and start compressions without delay.
Keep compressions going while the defibrillator charges and keep the pre-shock pause short.
Perform and call the safety check; never shock during manual compressions.
